## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:

content.text:
# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment.

- Timer per dare with countdown, pause/resume, start button. Some dares are "hold for X seconds".

Maybe "bonus" category-specific. Session length: 3 rounds per player? Could have goal options (quick 5 turns, 10 turns, endless). Simpler: each player gets 3 turns. Winner = most points. Or a "Dare Meter" target. Let's implement "3 rounds each" default, configurable maybe 1/3/5 turns per player.
- Single player: 10 dare run, score.
- Timer and controls: hold to skip? Use buttons.

Need ensure 100+ unique dares. We can generate 120 or 130. Categories:
- Ice (cold/chill): 12
- Clothespin: 12
- Pain Endurance (safe sensations): 12
- Silly: 15
- Social: 15
- Chaos: 10
- Focus: 10

Could make "House rules" toggles: timer on/off, sound on/off, intensity. Need not overcomplicate.

Visual design: vibrant dark neon arcade. Use Google Fonts? Network dependency maybe offline. Use system fonts with fallback, maybe @import from Google Fonts could fail offline. Better use local CSS with font stacks: "Trebuchet MS", etc. Could use display font via Google? No, keep self-contained. Use CSS with strong styling, gradients, noise, confetti canvas. Maybe use emoji icons.

Gameplay flow:
1. Title screen: logo, mode buttons Single Player / Group Mode, settings (intensity, categories, timer).
2. Setup modal/panel:
   - Single: name? optional; number of dares (5, 10, 15, open-ended). Start.

3. Game screen:

   - Should be playable without timer too.
   - Each turn, card flip animation.
   - Group: player strip with scores, active highlight.
   - Sound effects using Web Audio API (no external assets).

Maybe add "pass the device" interstitial for group to prevent seeing next dare? Actually dares aren't secret, no need.

Need "dares would not be repeated" explicit; track deck and show remaining count.

Include safety note about not clipping sensitive areas, max 20 seconds, no broken skin. Pain enduring: ice cubes, wall sit, plank, spicy candy, sour candy, rubber band snap? Rubber band snap can hurt; avoid. Use safe challenges: hold ice, wall sit, plank, breath hold? No breath holding. Cold shower? Avoid. Use "hold an ice cube in each hand for 20s", "wall sit 45s", "plank 30s", "sour candy 30s", "hot sauce drop on tongue (optional, with consent)"—safer to avoid hot sauce. "Eat a spoonful of wasabi"? Avoid. "Lemon wedge" safe. "Hold a cold can against your neck" etc. Also "sensation" dares: clothespin on earlobe, finger, shirt hem. Always include "10-second rule" and stop if pain. No skin-breaking.

ice, clip, endurance, silly, social, chaos, focus, movement, taste, sound.

Each dare has duration. Some no timer (duration 0/optional). The UI should display "No timer needed" if 0. Timer countdown. Timer should start at card reveal? Game mechanics:

Animations: 3D card flip, gradient orbs, confetti canvas, pulsing timer ring. Responsive.

Need maybe a "rules / safety" modal accessible from title screen; also display a compact safety line.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page

  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element

  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button

  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)

  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog

export const CATEGORY_KEYS = Object.keys(CATEGORIES);

export function daresFor({ categories, maxLevel = 3, playerCount = 1 } = {}) {
  const allowed = categories && categories.length ? new Set(categories) : new Set(CATEGORY_KEYS);
  return DARES.filter((dare) => (
    allowed.has(dare.cat)
    && dare.lvl <= maxLevel
    && (dare.min || 1) <= playerCount
  ));
}

export function shuffle(items, random = Math.random) {
  const copy = items.slice();
  for (let index = copy.length - 1; index > 0; index -= 1) {
    const swap = Math.floor(random() * (index + 1));
    [copy[index], copy[swap]] = [copy[swap], copy[index]];
  }
  return copy;
}

# Dare Deck

**Draw. Do. Survive.** A complete browser party game with 132 unique dares, ten categories, and zero repeats per run.

- **Solo run** — 5, 10, 15, or 20 dares, scored as you go.
- **Group mode** — 2–8 players, editable names, turn-by-turn play, live scoreboard, and a podium finish.
- **Categories** — Ice, Clothespin, Endurance, Silly, Social, Chaos, Focus, Movement, Taste, and Sound.
- **No repeats** — every drawn card leaves the deck. The run ends when the turns or the deck do.
- **Timers, pause/resume, safe-word skip, sound, and confetti** are built in. State fits phones and tablets.
- **Safety first** — consent, allergy checks, and stop rules are always in the House Rules dialog.

### Play locally

```sh
./start.sh          # serves the game on http://localhost:3000 (or $PORT)

## Objective
- Build and finish a complete, playable browser “dare game” requested by the user, with 100+ non-repeating dares, multiple dare types (ice, pain endurance, clothespin, etc.), and solo/group modes.

## Requirements
- More than 100 dares.
- Dares must not repeat during a run.
- Multiple categories/types, explicitly including ice, pain endurance/endurance, clothespin, etc.
- Support both single-player and group play.
- Build request: no clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when finished.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a dependency-free static HTML/CSS/ES-module web game.
- Created 132 unique dares across 10 categories: Ice, Clothespin, Endurance, Silly, Social, Chaos, Focus, Movement, Taste, Sound.
- “No repeats” enforced by shuffled deck + popping cards (removed once drawn).
- Solo mode: selectable 5/10/15/20 dares.
- Group mode: 2–8 editable players, selectable 1/2/3/5 turns each, live scoreboard, podium results.
- Intensity filter: Chill (level 1), Bold (level ≤2), Savage (all levels).
- Safety-first framing: consent, allergy checks, safe-word skip, no dangerous dares, stop rules in House Rules dialog.
- Added timers, pause/resume, scoring, streaks, skipping, chicken-outs, WebAudio sound, confetti, responsive mobile layout, localStorage lifetime stats.
- Removed expensive visual effects during performance debugging: animated blurred orbs, SVG grain turbulence, setup backdrop-filter, gradient mask border, large text-shadow.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` — home/setup/game/end screens, House Rules and Quit dialogs, controls, accessibility live region.
- `styles.css` — full responsive neon party-game visual system, card animations, timer rings, modals, podium, mobile/safe-area handling.
- `dares.js` — 132 unique dares, category metadata, intensity/player filtering, shuffle helper.
- `game.js` — full game loop, setup state, group turns, timers, scoring, results, sound, confetti, localStorage stats.
- `tests/dare-data.test.mjs` and `test.sh` — data integrity/no-repeat tests; currently pass.
- `README.md` — added game-specific overview and run/test instructions.
- Manual Playwright verification completed for desktop and mobile home, solo game, timed card, result overlay, group setup, group game, group end podium, and solo end screen.
- Test command `./test.sh` passes: `Dare data OK — 132 unique dares, 106 solo-friendly, 132 group-ready.`

### Active
- Optimizing first-paint performance so the default capture auto-start reliably clicks `#start-game` without Playwright “element is not stable” timeout.
- Just removed/reduced expensive home-screen visuals and was measuring performance changes; need to rerun the official capture script.

### Blocked
- `./capture.sh` currently fails before screenshots with:
  `locator.click: Timeout 2000ms exceeded` / `element is not stable` while clicking `Start`.
- Root cause narrowed to ~2–4.5s software-rendered first paint; body radial gradients and heavy effects were major contributors. Some optimizations applied but not yet revalidated with `capture.sh`.

## Next Move
1. Re-measure home first-paint/performance after latest CSS changes.
2. Run `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots/final ./capture.sh` and confirm auto-start + both desktop/mobile screenshots.
3. If capture still times out, further simplify remaining heavy home effects (large box-shadows, `.deck-fan`, remaining backdrop/blur effects) or redesign background/panels with cheaper linear gradients.
4. Re-run `./test.sh` and a quick Playwright smoke test after any changes.
5. Take fresh final desktop/mobile screenshots and inspect them.
6. Verify git diff/file state; leave changes uncommitted unless workflow requires otherwise.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: game shell, all screens/dialogs, Start button.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: visual system; currently mid-performance optimization.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: complete game logic; contains `window.__dareDeck` debug API.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/dares.js`: 132-dare library and filters.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/dare-data.test.mjs`: data/no-repeat assertions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/test.sh`: runs the data test.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md`: project overview updated.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: manual verification screenshots; `screenshots/final/` is currently empty after failed capture.
- `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-capture.mjs`: official capture behavior.
- `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/capture-start.mjs`: auto-click logic requiring a single exact “Start” button and element stability.

## Important Context
- Dev server is running in tmux session `daredeck` on port `3002`, command roughly:
  `PORT=3002 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"`.
- Start button text must remain exactly `Start` for auto-capture; only one such button can match.
- Playwright browser was installed via `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`; default viewport used by CLI was `1050x793`, official capture uses `1440x900` and `390x844`.
- `capture.sh` failed with “element is not stable”; direct Playwright debug showed first-frame stalls of ~2.3–4.5s under SwiftShader, while blank page is ~0.3–0.4s.
- Earlier tests confirmed:
  - no repeats across an 8+ card browser run;
  - timer, pause/resume, scoring, group rotation, podium, mobile layout all work;
  - console had 0 errors before latest CSS edits.
- `window.__dareDeck` exposes `{ game, DARES, CATEGORIES, startGame, daresFor }` for automated checks.
- Latest CSS edits removed `.backdrop`/orb HTML and CSS, replaced body radial gradients with linear gradients, removed `.setup` backdrop-filter and gradient-mask pseudo-element, reduced large text-shadow, and removed animated orbs/grain. These changes are uncommitted.

content.text:
# PlayGround

# Dare Deck

**Draw. Do. Survive.** A complete browser party game with 132 unique dares, ten categories, and zero repeats per run.

- **Solo run** — 5, 10, 15, or 20 dares, scored as you go.
- **Group mode** — 2–8 players, editable names, turn-by-turn play, live scoreboard, and a podium finish.
- **Categories** — Ice, Clothespin, Endurance, Silly, Social, Chaos, Focus, Movement, Taste, and Sound.
- **No repeats** — every drawn card leaves the deck. The run ends when the turns or the deck do.
- **Timers, pause/resume, safe-word skip, sound, and confetti** are built in. State fits phones and tablets.
- **Safety first** — consent, allergy checks, and stop rules are always in the House Rules dialog.

### Play locally

```sh
./start.sh          # serves the game on http://localhost:3000 (or $PORT)
./test.sh           # validates the dare library and no-repeat draw logic
```

No build step or dependencies. Everything is plain HTML, CSS, and ES modules.

### Project files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `index.html` | All screens, dialogs, and game shell |
| `styles.css` | Responsive visual system |
| `dares.js` | 132-dare library, categories, filtering, shuffle |
| `game.js` | Setup, turns, timers, scoring, results, sound, confetti |
| `tests/dare-data.test.mjs` | Data integrity and deck checks |

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

jobs:
